summary: Remote WebSocket gateway drives local PTY/shell execution on the installer host
details: The @whalent/agent CLI daemon opens a persistent WebSocket connection to a remote gateway (default wss://memory.whalent.com, overridable via --gateway) and routes messages from that gateway into local process execution on the host running the daemon. The package declares `ws`, `@xterm/headless`, and optional `node-pty` as dependencies, and the obfuscated `dist/core.cjs` bundle contains WebSocket handlers combined with `spawn(` and xterm-headless code paths. The README documents that the daemon accepts remote commands (including upgrade and restart) via the gateway and auto-starts workers. Whoever controls the gateway endpoint therefore has arbitrary command execution and interactive terminal capability on any host where the daemon is running, for the lifetime of the daemon. The main entrypoint `dist/index.cjs` and `dist/core.cjs` (~14MB) are shipped as javascript-obfuscator output (string-array rotation, RC4-style decoder, control-flow flattening, hex-named identifiers), which prevents inspection of the exact set of commands the gateway is authorized to issue and under what conditions. The daemon is started by explicit user invocation of the `whalent` bin rather than a lifecycle hook, so remote command execution does not fire on `npm install`; however, once started (the package's documented mode of use), the host is under remote-party control via the gateway.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
